title: CAQH (now DataSpring): The Hidden Causes of Inaccurate Provider Directories (white paper on a 2019 survey of 1,240 physician practices)

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: CAQH / DataSpring (nonprofit that operates the Provider Data Portal and sells provider data and directory solutions)
source_type: Industry organization white paper reporting its own practice survey (n=1,240, September 2019)
reliability: Interested party: the publisher operates and sells the single-platform provider data service whose savings it estimates. Survey method is summarized only briefly in the paper.
findings: A September 2019 survey of 1,240 physician practices found the average practice has 20.2 health plan contracts (13.5 for practices with fewer than 5 providers).

Authors report practices spend at least one full staff day per week on directory maintenance, at an average cost of $998.84 per month per practice ($319.46 per month for practices with fewer than 5 providers); average fully loaded staff cost used is $63,004.
Authors extrapolate the cost to $2.76 billion per year across US physician practices.

Respondents using a single platform to exchange credentialing information reported $1,249.86 per month in associated administrative costs, 39.6 percent less than the $2,068.00 per month reported by those using multiple approaches; authors project a saving of $396 per month ($4,746 per year) per practice and at least $1.1 billion nationwide, "assuming similar efficiencies".

Citing a 2018 AMA survey, the paper says directory information is submitted by fax (38%), credentialing software (13%), email (13%), provider management and enrollment software (5%), and phone, mail and other methods (14%).
The paper states CMS requires Medicare Advantage plans to contact providers quarterly, and cites Berkeley Research Group for 19 states requiring at least monthly directory updates.
limitations: Survey data are from September 2019 and are more than six years old; the PDF itself carries a later "last updated" stamp (2026) with no restated data.
Publication date not shown in the document, so the published field is null.
Cost figures are survey-reported or modelled estimates; the questionnaire, response rate and how time was converted to dollars are not given.
The single-platform saving is a projection by a party that sells such a platform; the paper footnotes it as likely conservative but gives no measured outcome.
The 2023 and 2024 CAQH Index reports were downloaded and searched; they do not report credentialing or directory cost per transaction, so no Index figures are used.
Cost excludes credentialing/enrollment applications themselves; focuses on directory maintenance.
